meta.title: Arabic Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 164 expressions · 58 everyday, 68 idioms, 38 proverbs · both directions
meta.desc: 164 Arabic set phrases, idioms and proverbs of Modern Standard Arabic, in three subdecks: 58 everyday phrases, 68 idioms and 38 proverbs. Both study directions come as two cards of one expression — Arabic → English and English → Arabic — each with a schedule of its own. This is a companion to the five level decks, Arabic A1 to C1, and not one of them: a level is an inventory of words, and an expression is a unit a list of words cannot see. Nothing here is taught by any of the five, so the two can be studied together without repeating an entry. The PHRASES are the formulas a speaker uses as one piece — the reply to a greeting, thanks, wishes for a feast or a birthday, condolences, and the everyday sayings of religious origin that any Arabic speaker uses socially (God knows; no power but God's). The IDIOMS are expressions whose meaning is not their words' (to save face, the tip of the iceberg), with the literal sense in brackets where it helps. The PROVERBS are complete sayings with a moral. WHAT IS LEFT OUT, since it matters: every expression here is an entry of the English Wiktionary, but not every entry is here. Formulas of worship and religious honorifics are not taught, nor Christian formulas, political slogans, phrasebook sentences a learner builds rather than learns, dialect, Classical-only and archaic entries, or near-duplicates. The English was written for this deck. Within each subdeck the expressions are ordered by how many of Tatoeba's Arabic sentences contain them, so the ones met most often come first. Real example sentences come with 26 of the 164, with the expression picked out in colour and a speaker beside it. Every headword is printed with its short vowels, and the romanisation beneath it is in Wiktionary's scheme (ā ī ū for the long vowels, ʔ for hamza, ʕ for ʿayn, a dot under the emphatic letters); 89 expressions Wiktionary does not romanise were romanised in the same scheme from their vowels. Vowelled forms and romanisations: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). The English meanings were written for this deck. Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
